column1: # MARKER CLASSES -- the family a marker belongs to, and what that family looks
# like by default.
# A row in markers.tsv names its class; the class supplies the default SHAPE and
# COLOUR, and the row overrides either one.
# ⭐ WHY CLASSES EXIST (DL J7, 2026-08-04). Every marker used to be a confidence
# claim, and that narrowness was genuinely the feature: you can ask "what is
# unconfirmed across this whole site" only while every row answers the same
# question. When terminology arrived it was nearly built as a SECOND, parallel
# family -- two mechanisms for one concept -- because the table had no way to say
# which KIND a row was. Michael's ruling: it IS a marker, put it in markers, you
# have found CLASSES. The report groups by class, so the confidence question stays
# answerable no matter how many glossary terms a site marks.
# ADDING A MARKER is a row in markers.tsv. ADDING A WHOLE FAMILY is a row here.
# Neither is a code change and neither is a CSS change -- the class colour is
# emitted as generated CSS by docrender/markers.py.
# COLUMNS
# class    the token a markers.tsv row names
# shape    default shape for the family: box · plain · strike · soft
# color    default colour: any token from EITHER colour table, or a literal
#          hex/oklch
# wash     BOX SHAPES ONLY. How much of the marker's own colour tints the chip
#          behind the text, as a percentage. BLANK inherits the 10% baked into
#          the `.dr-mark--box` fallback, so every existing family renders
#          byte-identically to before this column existed.
# label    what this family MEANS. For the reader of this file and the report.
# ⭐ `wash` EXISTS BECAUSE THE HIGHLIGHT FAMILY NEEDED A FIFTH SHAPE AND DID NOT
# GET ONE (2026-08-07). Michael asked for a highlighter that renders a box like
# `tbc` does. The chip ALREADY had a tinted ground -- `color-mix(... 10%,
# transparent)` -- so nothing was missing; 10% is simply below the threshold
# where a reader registers it as highlighting rather than as a border.
# The obvious move was a `mark` shape with a heavier tint. Rejected: the closed
# set of four is argued in THREE files on the grounds that a reader can tell four
# shapes apart at a glance and cannot tell nine, and "same shape, more tint" is
# not a new shape -- it is the same shape with a different number in it. ⚑ A
# request for a new VARIANT is a request for a new PARAMETER far more often than
# it is a request for a new KIND, and the tell is whether you can state the
# difference without using a number.
# ⚠️ WASH AND COLOUR ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT A FREE DIAL.
# The chip text sits on a wash of ITSELF, so raising the wash lowers the contrast
# between the two. markers.tsv's header already says to measure the chip and not
# the page; that warning now has a knob attached to it, so measure after changing
# this cell rather than after changing only `color`.
# 🔴 `terminology` ASKED FOR `accent-soft` FOR TWO DAYS AND NEVER GOT IT, AND THE
# COMMENT THAT USED TO SIT HERE EXPLAINED IT AS A PLAN. Two things were wrong.
# 1. THE VALIDATOR COULD NOT SEE IT. `_known_tokens()` read only the nine-token
#    stand-in, so every canonical token except `accent` and `warn` was refused --
#    reported unknown once per build and silently painted in the body colour.
#    Fixed 2026-08-05: the two tables are unioned.
# 2. RED AND `accent-soft` WAS THE WRONG TOKEN ANYWAY, which the fallback hid.
#    It is a tinted GROUND, not a text colour: on eos dark it is #1a2b42, a
#    near-black navy measuring 1.4:1 on the canvas. Had the validator accepted
#    it on the day it was written, the terminology marker would have rendered
#    invisible. The fallback to body colour is the only reason nobody noticed.
# ⚑ Worth keeping: A BROKEN REFERENCE THAT DEGRADES GRACEFULLY CAN HIDE A SECOND,
# WORSE MISTAKE UNDERNEATH IT. The report said "unknown token" and everyone read
# that as "not vendored yet" rather than "and also wrong."
# `accent-2` is the Eos TRACKED violet -- 6.63 dark / 5.81 light against the
# canvas -- and it is semantically right as well as legible: on the console it
# is the colour of a named, tracked value, which is exactly what a defined term
# is. ⭐ Still ONE CELL: the token is named here and nowhere else, so changing it
# again is a data edit. The moment a second surface hardcodes it, that is dead.
# ⚠️ `highlight` TAKES `accent` ON MICHAEL'S RULING, AGAINST MY RECOMMENDATION,
# AND HIS REASONING IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVES (2026-08-07). I argued for `accent-2`
# because `accent` already paints the `note` CALLOUT and a highlight is closer to
# the `abstract` register. He pointed out that `accent-2` already paints a MARKER
# -- terminology, one row below -- and that the callout collision costs nothing
# because a box and an inline chip are different surfaces a reader never compares.
# ⭐ THE GENERAL RULE, WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE IT DECIDES THE NEXT FAMILY TOO:
# COLOUR COLLISIONS ONLY COUNT WITHIN A SURFACE. Two callouts sharing a token is
# the documented design (`tip`/`success`/`good` all take `good`). Two INLINE
# MARKERS sharing one would be a genuine defect, because they appear in the same
# sentence, at the same size, and the only thing telling them apart is the paint.
# blocks.tsv can reuse freely; this file cannot.
# ⚠️ AND THE SEPARATION IS NOW LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN INCIDENTAL. `highlight`
# and `confidence` are the only two BOXED marker families, so their two tokens --
# `accent` and `warn` -- are the one pair on this whole surface that a reader has
# to distinguish mid-sentence. On the URITP palette that is #b38216 against
# #ffcc33: the same hue, ~40% apart in lightness, which is enough at 25% wash and
# is the thinnest margin in this file. 🚩 If a third boxed family is ever added,
# it does NOT get to pick a colour by taste -- measure it against both of these
# first, and Michael's note is that the hex is the free variable if it is tight.
class
confidence
